data.gender_notes: Aseem is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Aseem is derived from Sanskrit and means 'not far' or 'near'. It is a name rooted in Hindu mythology, referring to the god Indra who is believed to be close to his devotees. The name Aseem carries the meaning “Not far, near” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aseem usually hope their child will grow to embody not far, near and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Aseem belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Not far, near.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aseem total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

This could symbolize the bond between a parent and child, a couples' love and commitment, or the connection between a devotee and their deity. In Hindu culture, this name is associated with trust, loyalty, and being there for others through thick and thin.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Aseem carries deep meaning. It reminds us of the closeness and proximity of the divine, representing the inherent connection we all have to the divine. This name also encourages us to be present and fully engaged with the people and situations around us, recognizing the divine in all things. Another reference to Aseem is found in the Skanda Purana, where he is mentioned as a great devotee of Lord Shiva, who is known for his humility and asceticism.
